column3: Hebrew names sacrifices; BSB has the broader “feasting.”
Hebrew says “among brothers”; BSB supplies “as one of the brothers” and “his” before inheritance.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has singular “lip”; BSB has plural lips.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has plural sons and fathers in the second clause; BSB has a singular son and father.
Hebrew retains singular lip imagery in both clauses; BSB has eloquent words and lying lips.
Hebrew describes a stone of favor in its owners’ eyes; BSB has a charm to its giver.
Hebrew says “seeks love” and has a singular close companion; BSB has “promotes love” and plural friends.

“Better” is implicit rather than expressly stated in Hebrew’s comparison.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “water”; BSB specifies a flood.
Hebrew names the people acquitting and condemning; BSB uses the actions as subjects.
Hebrew says the fool has no heart; BSB interprets this as no intention of buying wisdom.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “before his neighbor,” rather than “for his neighbor,” and retains the image of lacking heart.
Hebrew says “seeks destruction”; BSB has “invites destruction.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says the heart does good for healing and has singular “bone”; BSB identifies it as medicine and uses plural bones.
Hebrew retains the image “from the bosom” and plural paths of justice; BSB has a covert bribe and a singular course.
Hebrew directly locates wisdom before the discerning man’s face and the eyes at earth’s end; BSB interprets focus and wandering.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has plural noble people; BSB has a singular noble.
The printed Hebrew describes a person noble in spirit; BSB has maintaining a calm spirit.
Hebrew says closing one’s lips; BSB has holding one’s tongue.
